title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — ज्ञानविज्ञानयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 7: Knowledge and Discernment
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/ज्ञानविज्ञानयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)

sentences.t:
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः ।
असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
sentences.tr:
mayi āsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogam yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ |
asaṃśayam samagram mām yathā jñāsyasi tat śṛṇu ||

morph.gloss: clung, attached (past participle of ā-sañj, first compound member)
mind (āsakta-manas: 'mind attached [to me]', nom. sg. masc.; mayi + ā- → mayyā-)
to yoke, discipline (oneself) (yuñjan: present participle 'practicing, disciplining', nom. sg.)
refuge, reliance (mad-āśraya: 'having me as refuge', nom. sg.)
without doubt, undoubtedly (adverbial acc. sg. neut.)
whole, entire, complete (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with mām)
to know (jñāsyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall know')
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., referring to the coming teaching; -t + ś- → -c ch-)

sentences.l: Mind attached to me, O son of Pṛthā, practicing yoga, having me as refuge — without doubt, completely, how you shall know me, that hear.
sentences.i: With your mind fixed on me, Pārtha, practicing yoga and relying on me, hear now how you shall know me completely, beyond all doubt.
sentences.n: This opens Kṛṣṇa's discourse proper, continuing without interruption from the end of chapter 6, and addressed throughout this chapter to Arjuna as Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā' (i.e. Kuntī). Sandhi: मय्यासक्तमनाः is mayi + āsakta-manāḥ (i + ā → yā); तच्छृणु is tat + śṛṇu (-t + ś- → -c ch-). Mad-āśrayaḥ, 'having me as refuge', anticipates the theme of surrender to Kṛṣṇa alone that runs through the whole chapter (cf. verse 14's māṃ eva ye prapadyante).

sentences.t:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
jñānam te aham sa-vijñānam idam vakṣyāmi aśeṣataḥ |
yat jñātvā na iha bhūyaḥ anyat jñātavyam avaśiṣyate ||

morph.gloss: knowledge (acc. sg. neut., object of vakṣyāmi)
I (nom. sg.; te + a- → te 'ha-, with avagraha)
discernment, realized knowledge (sa-vijñāna: 'together with discernment', acc. sg. neut.)
this (acc. sg. neut., in apposition to jñānam)
to speak, tell (vakṣyāmi: future 1st sg. 'I shall speak'; -i + a- → -y a-)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object of jñātvā; -t + j- → -j jñ-)
to know (jñātavya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut., predicate; anyat + j- → anyaj j-)
to remain over, be left (avaśiṣyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'remains')

sentences.l: Knowledge, together with discernment, to you I shall speak, this, completely; having known which, nothing further, other, here remains to be known.
sentences.i: I will teach you this knowledge in full, together with its realization, leaving nothing out; once you have known it, nothing further remains to be known here.
sentences.n: Jñāna and vijñāna, 'knowledge' and 'discernment' (its personally realized counterpart, per Śaṅkara — cf. 6.8's jñāna-vijñāna-tṛpta-ātmā), give this chapter its title, Jñāna-vijñāna-yoga; the promise that nothing further remains to be known once this teaching is grasped is fulfilled by the chapter's own subject, Kṛṣṇa's full nature. Sandhi: तेऽहं is te + aham; सविज्ञानमिदं is sa-vijñānam + idam (no fusion — final -m stays before a vowel); वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः is vakṣyāmi + aśeṣataḥ; यज्ज्ञात्वा is yat + jñātvā; नेह is na + iha; भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते packs bhūyaḥ + anyat + jñātavyam + avaśiṣyate.

sentences.t:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
sentences.tr:
manuṣyāṇām sahasreṣu kaścit yatati siddhaye |
yatatām api siddhānām kaścit mām vetti tattvataḥ ||

morph.gloss: someone (kaścit: nom. sg. masc.; -t + y- → -d y-)
accomplishment, success, perfection (dat. sg. of purpose, 'for perfection')
to strive (yatatām: present participle, gen. pl. 'of those striving')
someone (kaścit: nom. sg. masc.; -t + m- → -n m-)
reality, true nature (adverbial abl., 'in reality, truly')

sentences.l: Among thousands of men, someone strives for perfection; even among those striving [and] perfected, someone knows me in truth.
sentences.i: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection; and even among those who strive and succeed, scarcely one knows me in truth.
sentences.n: Kaścit ... kaścit, 'someone ... someone', doubled, understates the rarity rather than saying 'few' outright — tradition reads it as 'hardly anyone at all'. Sandhi: कश्चिद्यतति is kaścit + yatati (-t + y- → -d y-); कश्चिन्मां is kaścit + mām (-t + m- → -n m-).

sentences.t:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।
अहंकार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥
sentences.tr:
bhūmiḥ āpaḥ analaḥ vāyuḥ kham manaḥ buddhiḥ eva ca |
ahaṃkāraḥ iti iyam me bhinnā prakṛtiḥ aṣṭadhā ||

morph.gloss: water (āpaḥ: nom. pl., used collectively for the element; -iḥ + ā- → -ir ā-)
fire (nom. sg.; āpaḥ + analaḥ → āpo 'nalaḥ, -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha; -aḥ before v- of vāyuḥ → -o, written as a separate word)
ether, space, the sky (nom. sg. neut.)
ego, the sense of 'I' (lit. 'I-maker'; nom. sg.; visarga dropped before the vowel i- of iti)
thus (marks the close of the list)
this (iyam: nom. sg. fem., referring to prakṛtiḥ; iti + i- → itī-)
to split, divide (bhinnā: past participle 'divided, differentiated', nom. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtiḥ)
nature (nom. sg. fem., subject; -iḥ + a- → -ir a-)

sentences.l: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, and understanding too, and egoism — thus this, my nature, divided, eightfold.
sentences.i: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, understanding, and egoism — this is my nature, divided eight ways.
sentences.n: The first formal statement of prakṛti as eightfold: five gross elements (bhūmi, ap, anala, vāyu, kha), then manas, buddhi, and ahaṃkāra, 'ego, the sense of I' — together Kṛṣṇa's 'lower' nature, set against the 'higher' nature named in the next verse. Note that ahaṃkāra is here classed as a product of nature, not as the self. Sandhi across the list: bhūmiḥ+āpaḥ→bhūmir āpaḥ; āpaḥ+analaḥ→āpo'nalaḥ; manaḥ+buddhiḥ→mano buddhiḥ; buddhiḥ+eva→buddhir eva; iti+iyam→itīyam; prakṛtiḥ+aṣṭadhā→prakṛtir aṣṭadhā.

sentences.t:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् ।
जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥
sentences.tr:
aparā iyam itaḥ tu anyām prakṛtim viddhi me parām |
jīva-bhūtām mahā-bāho yayā idam dhāryate jagat ||

morph.gloss: other, inferior, lower (aparā: nom. sg. fem., predicate; aparā + i- → apare-)
this (iyam: nom. sg. fem., subject, referring to the eightfold prakṛti of verse 4)
other, different (anyām: acc. sg. fem., object of viddhi, agreeing with prakṛtim; itaḥ + tu → itas tu; tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)
higher, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim)
life, the living/individual soul (first compound member)
become, having become (jīva-bhūta: 'become the individual soul, existing as life', acc. sg. fem., agreeing with parām prakṛtim)
which (yayā: instr. sg. fem. relative, referring to the higher prakṛti)
this (nom. sg. neut., referring to jagat; yayā + i- → yaye-)
to hold, support (causative dhāryate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is held up, is sustained')
the world, the universe (nom. sg. neut., subject)

sentences.l: This is the lower; but know as another, different [from] this, my higher nature — become the individual soul, O mighty-armed one, by which this world is sustained.
sentences.i: This is my lower nature; but know that I have another, higher nature besides it — existing as the individual soul, mighty-armed Arjuna, by which this universe is sustained.
sentences.n: Parā prakṛti, the 'higher nature', is defined as jīva-bhūtā, 'become the individual soul' — Śaṅkara identifies it with the kṣetrajña, the knower of the field, taken up at length in chapter 13 — and is set against the aparā, 'lower', eightfold material nature of verse 4. Sandhi: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां packs aparā + iyam (ā+i→e), + itaḥ, itaḥ+tu→itastu, tu+anyām→tvanyām (yaṇ sandhi, u→v); ययेदं is yayā + idam (ā+i→e).

sentences.t:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय ।
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥
sentences.tr:
etat-yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇi iti upadhāraya |
aham kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ tathā ||

morph.gloss: womb, source, origin (etad-yoni: 'having this as their source', nom. pl. neut., agreeing with bhūtāni; -t + y- → -d y-)
all (sarvāṇi: nom. pl. neut., agreeing with bhūtāni)
thus (closes the statement; sarvāṇi + i- → sarvāṇī-)
to hold in mind, understand (causative upadhāraya: imperative 2nd sg. 'understand!'; iti + u- → ity u-)
to arise, originate (prabhava: 'origin, source', nom. sg., predicate)
to dissolve (pralaya: 'dissolution', nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)

sentences.l: Having this as their source, all beings — thus understand; I of the whole world [am] the origin, and likewise the dissolution.
sentences.i: Understand that all beings have their source in this twofold nature of mine; I am the origin of the whole world, and its dissolution as well.
sentences.n: Etad-yonīni, 'having this as their source', sums up verses 4-5: everything that exists arises from Kṛṣṇa's own nature in both its aspects, lower and higher. Sandhi: एतद्योनीनि is etat + yoni (-t + y- → -d y-); सर्वाणीत्युपधारय packs sarvāṇi + iti + upadhāraya (i+i→ī; i+u→y u-); प्रलयस्तथा is pralayaḥ + tathā.

sentences.t:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किंचिदस्ति धनंजय ।
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
sentences.tr:
mattaḥ parataram na anyat kiṃcit asti dhanaṃjaya |
mayi sarvam idam protam sūtre maṇi-gaṇāḥ iva ||

morph.gloss: higher, supreme (parataram: comparative, acc. sg. neut., predicate 'higher, greater')
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg.; -t + a- → -d a-)
to weave, string together (protam: past participle 'strung', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
cluster, group (maṇi-gaṇa: 'clusters of jewels', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before i- → -ā)

sentences.l: Than me higher nothing else whatsoever exists, Winner-of-wealth; in me all this is strung, as clusters of jewels on a thread.
sentences.i: There is nothing whatsoever higher than me, Dhanaṃjaya; on me all this is strung, like clusters of jewels on a thread.
sentences.n: Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth', a recurring epithet of Arjuna (cf. 1.15, ch.2, ch.4) won for plundering wealth from defeated kings. The image of jewels strung on a thread (sūtre maṇi-gaṇāḥ iva) pictures the whole cosmos as held together by, and wholly dependent on, Kṛṣṇa as its one underlying support — concrete confirmation of verse 6's claim to be the origin and dissolution of everything. Sandhi: नान्यत्किंचिदस्ति packs na + anyat + kiṃcit + asti (a+a→ā; -t+a→-d a-).

sentences.t:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः ।
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥
sentences.tr:
rasaḥ aham apsu kaunteya prabhā asmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ |
praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣam nṛṣu ||

morph.gloss: taste, sap, essence (rasaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; prabhā + a- → prabhā-)
the sun (śaśi-sūrya: 'moon and sun', gen. dual)
the Veda (sarva-veda: 'all the Vedas', loc. pl.)
sound (nom. sg., predicate; traditionally the defining quality of ether)
manliness, human vigor (vṛddhi derivative of puruṣa 'man'; nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Sap I am in the waters, O son of Kuntī; light I am of moon and sun; the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether, manliness in men.
sentences.i: I am the taste in water, Kaunteya; I am the radiance of the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, the manly vigor in men.
sentences.n: A catalogue of self-manifestations opens here and runs through verse 11, each an instance of 'I am' — asmi recurs explicitly through vv.8-11 (prabhāsmi here; tejaś ca asmi and tapaś ca asmi, v.9; buddhir buddhimatām asmi, v.10; kāmaḥ asmi, v.11), and is left implicit only occasionally, as in tejas tejasvinām aham in v.10's second half. Praṇava, 'Om', is the syllable that opens Vedic recitation; śabda, 'sound', is traditionally the defining quality of ether (ākāśa) among the five elements. Sandhi: रसोऽहमप्सु is rasaḥ + aham + apsu; प्रभास्मि is prabhā + asmi.

sentences.t:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥
sentences.tr:
puṇyaḥ gandhaḥ pṛthivyām ca tejaḥ ca asmi vibhāvasau |
jīvanam sarva-bhūteṣu tapaḥ ca asmi tapasviṣu ||

morph.gloss: pure, fragrant, meritorious (nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ before g- → -o)
brilliance, radiance, fire (tejaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; ca + a- → cā-)
lit. 'possessing splendor', a name of Agni, fire (loc. sg.)
austerity, ascetic heat (tapaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; ca + a- → cā-)

sentences.l: Pure fragrance in the earth, and radiance I am in fire; life in all beings, and austerity I am in ascetics.
sentences.i: I am the pure fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in fire; I am the life in all beings and the austerity in ascetics.
sentences.n: Continues verse 8's catalogue with four more instances. Vibhāvasu, literally 'possessing splendor', is a standing epithet used as a name for Agni, fire. Sandhi: तेजश्चास्मि and तपश्चास्मि both pack X + ca + asmi (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-; ca+asmi→cāsmi).

sentences.t:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
bījam mām sarva-bhūtānām viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
buddhiḥ buddhimatām asmi tejaḥ tejasvinām aham ||

morph.gloss: eternal, everlasting (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bījam)
intellect, understanding (buddhiḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -iḥ + b- → -ir b-)
intelligent, possessing intellect (buddhimatām: gen. pl. 'of the intelligent')
brilliance (tejaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
brilliant, glorious (tejasvinām: gen. pl. 'of the brilliant')
I (nom. sg., subject, with an implied asmi carried over from the first half)

sentences.l: The seed of all beings, know me, O son of Pṛthā, [as] eternal; the intellect of the intelligent I am, the brilliance of the brilliant [am] I.
sentences.i: Know me, Pārtha, to be the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intellect of the intelligent, and the brilliance of the brilliant.
sentences.n: Bīja, 'seed', is the causal image of Kṛṣṇa as the eternal seed from which all beings grow, resumed at 9.18 and 14.4. Sandhi: बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि is buddhiḥ + buddhimatām + asmi (-iḥ+b-→-ir b-); तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् is tejaḥ + tejasvinām + aham (-aḥ+t-→-as t-), aham here carrying the sense of the asmi already used in the first half.

sentences.t:
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
sentences.tr:
balam balavatām ca aham kāma-rāga-vivarjitam |
dharma-aviruddhaḥ bhūteṣu kāmaḥ asmi bharata-ṛṣabha ||

morph.gloss: devoid of, free from (past participle of vi-vṛj; kāma-rāga-vivarjita: 'free from desire and attachment', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with balam)
not opposed, not contrary (dharma-aviruddha: 'not opposed to dharma', nom. sg. masc.; dharma + a- → dharmā-; -aḥ before bh- → -o)
desire (kāmaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative, addressed to Arjuna; a + ṛ- → ar-)

sentences.l: The strength of the strong, and I [am, that strength] free from desire and attachment; not opposed to dharma among beings, desire I am, O bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.i: And I am the strength of the strong, free from desire and passion; and in all beings I am the desire that is not opposed to dharma, bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.n: Bharatarṣabha, 'bull among the descendants of Bharata', a recurring epithet of Arjuna (already used in ch.3), here formed by sandhi bharata+ṛṣabha→bharatarṣabha, a+ṛ-→ar-. The verse distinguishes ordinary desire (kāma) — condemned elsewhere as the enemy, 3.37, 2.62-63 — from kāma dharma-aviruddhaḥ, 'desire not opposed to dharma', legitimate desire pursued within the bounds of right order, which Kṛṣṇa here claims as his own. Sandhi: चाहं is ca+aham; धर्माविरुद्धो is dharma+aviruddhaḥ; कामोऽस्मि is kāmaḥ+asmi.

sentences.t:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
sentences.tr:
ye ca eva sāttvikāḥ bhāvāḥ rājasāḥ tāmasāḥ ca ye |
mattaḥ eva iti tān viddhi na tu aham teṣu te mayi ||

morph.gloss: who, which (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative)
belonging to sattva, of the nature of sattva (nom. pl. masc.; sattva kept untranslated as guṇa-vocabulary; -āḥ before bh- → -ā)
state, disposition, nature (nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ before r- → -ā)
belonging to rajas (nom. pl. masc.; rajas kept untranslated as guṇa-vocabulary; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
belonging to tamas (nom. pl. masc.; tamas kept untranslated as guṇa-vocabulary; -āḥ + c- → -āś c-)
which (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative, repeated)
me (mattaḥ: abl. sg. 'from me, out of me'; visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva)
thus (closes the statement; eva + i- → eve-)
that, they (tān: acc. pl. masc., object of viddhi, referring to bhāvāḥ)
I (nom. sg.; tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)

sentences.l: Which indeed are states of sattva, and of rajas and of tamas — know them as from me alone; but I [am] not in them, they [are] in me.
sentences.i: Whatever states of being there are — of sattva, of rajas, or of tamas — know that all of them come from me alone; but I am not in them; they are in me.
sentences.n: Sāttvika, rājasa, tāmasa, formed from the three guṇas, are the poem's first mention of all three together by name, ahead of their systematic treatment from chapter 14 on; guṇa and its derivatives stay untranslated per convention. The paradox mattaḥ eva ... na tv ahaṃ teṣu, 'from me alone ... yet I am not in them', is developed in the next verse and echoes the fuller formula at 9.4-5. Sandhi: चैव is ca+eva; राजसास्तामसाश्च is rājasāḥ+tāmasāḥ+ca; मत्त एवेति is mattaḥ+eva+iti (visarga silently dropped before the vowel of eva); त्वहं is tu+aham (yaṇ sandhi, u→v).

sentences.t:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
tribhiḥ guṇa-mayaiḥ bhāvaiḥ ebhiḥ sarvam idam jagat |
mohitam na abhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam ||

morph.gloss: one of the three guṇas, kept untranslated (first compound member)
made of, consisting of (suffix; guṇa-maya: 'made of the guṇas', instr. pl.; -aiḥ + bh- → -air bh-)
this (nom. sg. neut., subject, 'all this world')
world (nom. sg. neut., in apposition to sarvam idam)
to be deluded, confused (mohitam: past participle 'deluded', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat)
this (ebhyaḥ: abl. pl. 'than these', referring to the three guṇas' states)
higher, supreme (param: acc. sg., agreeing with mām)
imperishable, unchanging (avyayam: acc. sg., agreeing with mām)

sentences.l: By these three states made of the guṇas, all this world, deluded, does not recognize me, beyond these, the supreme, the imperishable.
sentences.i: Deluded by these three states made of the guṇas, this whole world fails to recognize me, who am beyond them, supreme and imperishable.
sentences.n: Guṇa-mayaiḥ bhāvaiḥ, 'states made of the guṇas', names the sāttvika, rājasa and tāmasa states of verse 12; guṇa stays untranslated while the suffix '-maya' ('made of, consisting of') is translated. The verse states the paradox of verse 12 from the world's side: deceived by what the guṇas produce, it fails to recognize Kṛṣṇa as param avyayam, 'beyond these, imperishable' — the veiling power named directly as māyā in the next verse. Sandhi: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः packs tribhiḥ+guṇamayaiḥ+bhāvaiḥ+ebhiḥ; नाभिजानाति is na+abhijānāti.

sentences.t:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
sentences.tr:
daivī hi eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā |
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etām taranti te ||

morph.gloss: divine (daivī: nom. sg. fem., agreeing with māyā)
for, indeed (hi + e- → hye-, yaṇ sandhi i → y)
this (eṣā: nom. sg. fem., referring to māyā)
one of the three guṇas, kept untranslated (first compound member)
made of, consisting of (suffix; guṇa-mayī: 'made of the guṇas', nom. sg. fem., agreeing with māyā)
illusion, power of illusion (nom. sg., subject)
to cross over, overcome (atyaya: 'crossing over, transcending'; dur-atyaya: 'hard to cross over', nom. sg. fem., agreeing with māyā)
to resort to, take refuge in (prapadyante: present middle 3rd pl.)
this (etām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with māyām)

sentences.l: Divine indeed [is] this, made of the guṇas, my illusion, hard to cross over; me alone who resort to, this illusion they cross over, they.
sentences.i: This divine illusion of mine, made of the guṇas, is hard to overcome; but those who take refuge in me alone cross over this illusion.
sentences.n: Māyā, rendered 'illusion' per Monier-Williams, is deliberately translated here — unlike guṇa, dharma, yoga, brahman and sāṃkhya, which stay untranslated: daivī ... guṇamayī māyā, 'this divine illusion of mine, made of the guṇas', names the veiling power that verse 13 described impersonally, now claimed as Kṛṣṇa's own (mama) and called durat-yayā, 'hard to cross over'. The one way past it is stated directly, māṃ eva ye prapadyante, 'those who take refuge in me alone', anticipating the fourfold classification of devotees beginning at verse 16. Sandhi: ह्येषा is hi+eṣā (i+e→ye, yaṇ sandhi).

sentences.t:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
sentences.tr:
na mām duṣkṛtinaḥ mūḍhāḥ prapadyante nara-adhamāḥ |
māyayā apahṛta-jñānāḥ āsuram bhāvam āśritāḥ ||

morph.gloss: to be deluded (mūḍha: past participle 'deluded, foolish', nom. pl.)
to resort to, take refuge in (prapadyante: present middle 3rd pl.)
lowest (nara-adhama: 'lowest of men', nom. pl.; nara + a- → narā-)
to carry off, rob (apahṛta: past participle, first compound member)
knowledge (apahṛta-jñāna: 'whose knowledge is robbed', nom. pl. masc., bahuvrīhi; māyayā + a- → māyayā-; -āḥ before ā- → -ā)
demonic, of the demons (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bhāvam)
state, nature (bhāvam: acc. sg. neut., object of āśritāḥ)
to resort to, take refuge in (āśrita: past participle 'having resorted to', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: Not me evil-doers, deluded, lowest of men, resort to — by illusion robbed of knowledge, having resorted to a demonic nature.
sentences.i: Evil-doers do not resort to me — deluded men, the lowest of mankind, their knowledge robbed by illusion, given over to a demonic nature.
sentences.n: This gives the negative counterpart to verse 14's promise: duṣkṛtinaḥ, 'evil-doers', are māyayā apahṛta-jñānāḥ, 'whose knowledge illusion has carried off' — the same illusion of verse 14, here at its most destructive — because they have instead āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ, 'taken refuge in a demonic nature', foreshadowing the fuller contrast of divine and demonic natures in chapter 16. Sandhi: दुष्कृतिनो is duṣkṛtinaḥ (-aḥ before m-→-o); नराधमाः is nara+adhamāḥ (a+a→ā); माययापहृतज्ञाना is māyayā+apahṛta-jñānāḥ.

sentences.t:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन ।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
sentences.tr:
catur-vidhāḥ bhajante mām janāḥ sukṛtinaḥ arjuna |
ārtaḥ jijñāsuḥ artha-arthī jñānī ca bharata-ṛṣabha ||

morph.gloss: kind, sort (catur-vidha: 'fourfold', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before bh- → -ā)
to worship, revere (bhajante: present middle 3rd pl.)
virtuous, of good deeds (nom. pl. masc., agreeing with janāḥ; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to be afflicted, distressed (ārta: past participle 'the distressed one', nom. sg.; -aḥ before j- → -o)
to know (jijñāsu: desiderative adjective 'desiring to know', nom. sg.; -uḥ + a- → -ur a-)
seeking, desirous of (artha-arthin: 'seeker of gain', nom. sg.; artha + a- → arthā-)
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative, repeated from verse 11)

sentences.l: Fourfold worship me, people meritorious, O Arjuna: the distressed, the desirous-of-knowledge, the seeker-of-gain, and the man of knowledge, O bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.i: Four kinds of virtuous people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of wisdom, bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.n: This opens the classic fourfold classification of devotees, developed through verse 19: ārta, 'the distressed'; jijñāsu, 'one desiring to know'; artha-arthī, 'one seeking [worldly] gain'; and jñānī, 'the man of knowledge' — all called sukṛtinaḥ, 'of good deeds', since even self-interested worship of Kṛṣṇa presupposes merit. Sandhi: सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन is sukṛtinaḥ+arjuna; जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी packs jijñāsuḥ+artha+arthī.

sentences.t:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
sentences.tr:
teṣām jñānī nitya-yuktaḥ eka-bhaktiḥ viśiṣyate |
priyaḥ hi jñāninaḥ atyartham aham saḥ ca mama priyaḥ ||

morph.gloss: they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'of them, among them')
the man of knowledge (nom. sg., subject)
disciplined, joined (nitya-yukta: 'ever disciplined', nom. sg.; visarga dropped before the vowel e- of ekabhaktiḥ)
devotion (eka-bhakti: 'of single devotion', nom. sg.; -iḥ + v- → -ir v-)
to excel, be distinguished (viśiṣyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is distinguished, excels')
man of knowledge (jñāninaḥ: gen. sg. 'to the man of knowledge'; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before the consonant c-)

sentences.l: Of these, the man of knowledge, ever disciplined, of single devotion, excels; dear indeed to the man of knowledge exceedingly [am] I, and he [is] dear to me.
sentences.i: Of these, the man of knowledge, ever disciplined and singly devoted, is supreme; for I am exceedingly dear to the man of knowledge, and he is dear to me.
sentences.n: This ranks the jñānī highest of the four types named in verse 16, describing him as nitya-yuktaḥ eka-bhaktiḥ, 'constantly disciplined, of single-minded devotion'; the mutual bond of dearness (priyaḥ ... priyaḥ) between Kṛṣṇa and the wise devotee is pressed further in verse 18 and echoes the later catalogue of 12.14-20. Sandhi: एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते is eka-bhaktiḥ+viśiṣyate; ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं is jñāninaḥ+atyartham+aham.

sentences.t:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् ।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
udārāḥ sarva eva ete jñānī tu ātmā eva me matam |
āsthitaḥ saḥ hi yukta-ātmā mām eva anuttamām gatim ||

morph.gloss: all (used here for the expected pronominal plural sarve, agreeing with ete: 'all of these'; an epic-Sanskrit spelling found throughout the manuscript tradition of this verse)
this (ete: nom. pl. masc. 'these'; eva + e- → evai-)
the man of knowledge (nom. sg., subject)
self (ātmā: nom. sg., predicate; tu + ā- → tvā-, yaṇ sandhi)
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'my, in my [view]')
to think, consider (mata: past participle 'considered, held to be', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
to stand firm in, be grounded in (āsthita: past participle 'grounded, established', nom. sg.)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before h-)
self (yukta-ātman: 'of disciplined self', nom. sg.; yukta + ā- → yuktā-)
unsurpassed, highest (anuttamām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim; eva + a- → evā-)
course, goal (acc. sg., in apposition to mām)

sentences.l: Noble indeed [are] all these; but the man of knowledge — [he is] my very self, [that is] my view; he, for, of disciplined self, is grounded in me alone [as] the highest goal.
sentences.i: All of these are noble, but the man of knowledge I hold to be my very self; for he, his self disciplined, is grounded in me alone as the highest goal.
sentences.n: This ranks the jñānī above the other three types of verse 16 in the strongest terms yet: ātmā eva me matam, 'he is, in my view, my very self' — identity language beyond even verse 17's mutual dearness. A textual note: the expected pronominal plural sarve, agreeing with ete, 'these', here appears in the manuscript tradition as bare sarva; the sense, 'all of these', is unaffected. Sandhi: एवैते is eva+ete (a+e→ai); त्वात्मैव is tu+ātmā+eva (yaṇ sandhi u→v; ā+e→ai); मामेवानुत्तमां is mām+eva+anuttamām (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते ।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥
sentences.tr:
bahūnām janmanām ante jñānavān mām prapadyate |
vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti saḥ mahā-ātmā su-durlabhaḥ ||

morph.gloss: possessing knowledge, wise (jñānavān: nom. sg. masc., subject)
to resort to, take refuge in (prapadyate: present middle 3rd sg.)
'son of Vasudeva', a name of Kṛṣṇa (nom. sg., predicate; the poem's most quoted formula, vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti)
all, everything (sarvam: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before m-)
self, soul (mahā-ātman: 'great-souled', nom. sg.; mahā + ā- → mahā-)
hard to obtain, rare (su-durlabha: 'very hard to find', nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge resorts to me, [thinking] 'the son of Vasudeva is everything' — thus; he, the great-souled one, is very hard to find.
sentences.i: After many births, the wise man takes refuge in me, realizing that Vāsudeva is everything; such a great soul is very rare.
sentences.n: Vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti, 'the son of Vasudeva is everything' (or 'all this is Vāsudeva'), is the chapter's most quoted line: Kṛṣṇa's own patronymic, Vāsudeva, is here identified with the totality of existence — the culminating realization of the jñānī praised in verses 17-18. Sandhi: सर्वमिति is sarvam+iti; स is saḥ before m- (visarga dropped).

sentences.t:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः ।
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
sentences.tr:
kāmaiḥ taiḥ taiḥ hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante anya-devatāḥ |
tam tam niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā ||

morph.gloss: that (taiḥ taiḥ: instr. pl., doubled for distribution, 'by these and those'; -aiḥ + t- → -ais t- twice)
to carry off (hṛta: past participle, first compound member; -aiḥ + h- → -air h-)
knowledge (hṛta-jñāna: 'whose knowledge is carried off', nom. pl. masc., bahuvrīhi)
to resort to, take refuge in (prapadyante: present middle 3rd pl.; prapadyante + anya- → prapadyante 'nya-)
that (tam: acc. sg. masc., doubled for distribution)
to restrain, observe (niyama: 'rule, observance, vow', acc. sg., object of āsthāya)
to adopt, resort to (āsthāya: gerund 'having adopted')
to restrain, govern (niyata: past participle 'constrained, governed', nom. pl.)
one's own (instr. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtyā)

sentences.l: By these and those desires robbed of knowledge, they resort to other deities, having adopted this or that observance, constrained by their own nature.
sentences.i: Those whose understanding is carried off by one desire or another resort to other deities, adopting this or that observance, driven by their own nature.
sentences.n: This turns to worship of 'other deities' as the counterpart to the jñānī's realization in verse 19: kāmaiḥ taiḥ taiḥ hṛta-jñānāḥ, 'whose knowledge is carried off by these various desires', echoes verse 15's māyayā apahṛta-jñānāḥ, but here the cause is named as desire rather than illusion outright, and the outcome is not irreligion but its diversion toward lesser objects — still ultimately Kṛṣṇa's own doing, as the next verse explains. Sandhi: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः packs kāmaiḥ+taiḥ+taiḥ+hṛta-jñānāḥ; प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः is prapadyante+anya-devatāḥ.

sentences.t:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति ।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ yaḥ yām yām tanum bhaktaḥ śraddhayā arcitum icchati |
tasya tasya acalām śraddhām tām eva vidadhāmi aham ||

morph.gloss: who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, doubled for distribution; -aḥ before y- → -o)
which (yām: acc. sg. fem. relative, doubled for distribution)
to worship (arcitum: infinitive 'to worship'; śraddhayā + a- → śraddhayā-)
to wish (icchati: present 3rd sg.; arcitum + i- → arcitumi-)
of him, of whatever [devotee] (tasya: gen. sg., doubled for distribution)
unwavering, unmoving (acalām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with śraddhām; tasya + a- → tasyā-)
that (tām: acc. sg. fem., in apposition to śraddhām)
to bestow, ordain, make firm (vidadhāmi: present 1st sg. 'I make firm, I grant'; -i + a- → -y a-)

sentences.l: Whatever devotee whatever form with faith wishes to worship, of that one that unwavering faith, that very [faith] I make firm, I.
sentences.i: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, that very faith of his I make firm and unwavering.
sentences.n: Yo yo ... yāṃ yāṃ ... tasya tasya, doubled relatives across both lines, are the standard Sanskrit distributive construction, 'whoever ... whatever ... of each such person': whatever deity's form a devotee approaches with faith, Kṛṣṇa himself is the one who grants and steadies that faith — the doctrine behind verse 20's worship of other deities. Sandhi: श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति packs śraddhayā+arcitum+icchati; तस्याचलां is tasya+acalām (a+a→ā); विदधाम्यहम् is vidadhāmi+aham (-i+a→-y a-).

sentences.t:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते ।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥
sentences.tr:
saḥ tayā śraddhayā yuktaḥ tasya ārādhanam īhate |
labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayā eva vihitān hi tān ||

morph.gloss: he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before t-)
endowed with, joined (yuktaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that (tasya: gen. sg., referring to the deity's form worshipped; tasya + ā- → tasyā-)
to propitiate, worship (ārādhana: 'worship, propitiation', acc. sg., object of īhate)
to seek, strive for (īhate: present middle 3rd sg.)
to obtain, gain (labhate: present middle 3rd sg.)
desire (kāmān: acc. pl., object of labhate)
I (mayā: instr. sg. 'by me'; mayā + e- → mayai-)
to grant, bestow, ordain (vihita: past participle 'granted', acc. pl. masc., agreeing with kāmān)
those (tān: acc. pl. masc., in apposition to kāmān)

sentences.l: He, endowed with that faith, seeks the worship of that [deity], and obtains thereby [his] desires, granted by me alone indeed, those.
sentences.i: Endowed with that faith, he seeks to worship that deity, and thereby obtains what he desires — desires granted, in truth, by me alone.
sentences.n: This continues verse 21: the devotee, steadied in faith, does obtain what he seeks from the lesser deity, but the verse insists mayaiva vihitān, 'granted by me alone' — that the fruit of any such worship still ultimately comes from Kṛṣṇa, the hidden source behind every deity, a claim made explicit in the next verse. Sandhi: युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते packs yuktaḥ+tasya+ārādhanam+īhate; कामान्मयैव is kāmān+mayā+eva (ā+e→ai).

sentences.t:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् ।
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥
sentences.tr:
antavat tu phalam teṣām tat bhavati alpa-medhasām |
devān deva-yajaḥ yānti mad-bhaktāḥ yānti mām api ||

morph.gloss: having an end, finite (antavat: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject, referring to phalam; -t + bh- → -d bh-)
to be, become (bhavati: present 3rd sg.; -i + a- → -y a-)
intelligence, wisdom (alpa-medhas: 'of little intelligence', gen. pl.)
god, deity (devān: acc. pl., object of yānti)
to worship, sacrifice to (deva-yaja: 'a worshipper of the gods', nom. pl.; -aḥ before y- → -o)
devotee (mad-bhakta: 'my devotees', nom. pl.; -āḥ before y- → -ā)

sentences.l: Finite, however, [is] the fruit of them; that comes to be for those of little intelligence; the worshippers of the gods go to the gods, my devotees go to me also.
sentences.i: But the fruit for such people is finite; it belongs to those of little intelligence: worshippers of the gods go to the gods, but my devotees come to me.
sentences.n: This states plainly what verses 20-22 implied: worship of 'other deities', though ultimately granted through Kṛṣṇa, yields only antavat phalam, 'a finite result', fit for alpa-medhasām, 'those of little understanding' — contrasted with mad-bhaktāḥ, 'my devotees', who reach Kṛṣṇa himself rather than a lesser heaven. Sandhi: अन्तवत्तु is antavat+tu; तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् packs tat+bhavati+alpa-medhasām; देवान्देवयजो is devān+deva-yajaḥ; मद्भक्ता is mat+bhaktāḥ.

sentences.t:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः ।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥
sentences.tr:
avyaktam vyaktim āpannam manyante mām abuddhayaḥ |
param bhāvam ajānantaḥ mama avyayam anuttamam ||

morph.gloss: unmanifest (acc. sg. neut., in apposition to mām)
manifestation, visible existence (vyaktim: acc. sg., object of āpannam)
to attain, arrive at (āpanna: past participle 'having attained', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with avyaktam; vyaktim + ā- → vyaktimā-)
to think, consider (manyante: present middle 3rd pl.)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of manyante)
unwise, lacking understanding (abuddhayaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)
higher, supreme (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bhāvam)
state, nature, being (bhāvam: acc. sg., object of ajānantaḥ)
not to know (ajānat: negative present participle 'not knowing', nom. pl., agreeing with abuddhayaḥ; -aḥ before m- → -o)
imperishable (avyayam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bhāvam; mama + a- → mamā-)
unsurpassed, highest (anuttamam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with bhāvam)

sentences.l: The unmanifest, having attained manifestation, unwise men think of me — not knowing my higher state, imperishable, unsurpassed.
sentences.i: Unwise men think of me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifest existence — not knowing my higher nature, imperishable and unsurpassed.
sentences.n: This criticizes those who take Kṛṣṇa's avatāra-appearance (cf. 4.6's ātma-māyā) for an ordinary change from unmanifest to manifest, missing his param bhāvam, 'higher nature' — avyayam anuttamam, 'imperishable, unsurpassed' — which no apparent birth touches, a point sharpened in verse 25's nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya. Sandhi: ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् packs mama+avyayam+anuttamam (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
na aham prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ |
mūḍhaḥ ayam na abhijānāti lokaḥ mām ajam avyayam ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject; na + a- → nā-)
to shine forth, be manifest (prakāśa: 'manifest, evident', nom. sg., predicate)
illusion, power of illusion (yoga-māyā: 'the power of illusion exercised through yoga', second member)
to envelop, cover (samāvṛta: past participle 'veiled, enveloped', nom. sg., agreeing with the implied 'I')
to be deluded (mūḍha: past participle, nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., referring to lokaḥ)
the world (nom. sg., subject; -aḥ before m- → -o)
unborn (ajam: acc. sg., agreeing with mām)
imperishable (avyayam: acc. sg., agreeing with mām)

sentences.l: Not I [am] manifest to all, veiled by [my] power of illusion exercised through yoga; this deluded world does not recognize me, unborn, imperishable.
sentences.i: I am not manifest to all, veiled as I am by my power of illusion exercised through yoga; this deluded world does not recognize me, the unborn, the imperishable.
sentences.n: Yoga-māyā, 'the power of illusion exercised through yoga', names the mechanism behind verse 24's error: Kṛṣṇa is hidden from ordinary sight not by any real birth or change but by his own concealing power, called māyā at verse 14 and here specified as wielded through yoga. Ajam avyayam, 'unborn, imperishable', restates verse 24's avyayam anuttamam in the poem's standard terms for what undergoes no birth or change, echoing 4.6's ajaḥ api san. Sandhi: नाहं is na+aham; मूढोऽयं is mūḍhaḥ+ayam; नाभिजानाति is na+abhijānāti.

sentences.t:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन ।
भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
sentences.tr:
veda aham samatītāni vartamānāni ca arjuna |
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni mām tu veda na kaścana ||

morph.gloss: to know (veda: perfect used as present, 1st sg. 'I know')
completely past, gone by (samatīta: acc. pl. neut., agreeing with bhūtāni)
to exist, be (vartamāna: present participle 'existing now, present', acc. pl. neut.)
to be (bhaviṣyat: future participle 'about to be, future', acc. pl. neut.)
being, creature (acc. pl. neut., object of veda)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of veda)
to know (veda: perfect used as present, 3rd sg. 'knows')
anyone, anyone at all (nom. sg.; with na: 'no one at all')

sentences.l: I know past, present, and future beings, Arjuna; but me no one at all knows.
sentences.i: I know all beings, Arjuna — past, present and to come; but no one knows me.
sentences.n: Vedāham ... na tu veda kaścana plays on two senses of vid, 'to know': Kṛṣṇa's own knowledge spans all three times, yet he himself remains unknown to anyone — the same hiddenness as verses 24-25, now stated as a general asymmetry rather than a matter of illusion specifically, and the premise for verses 27-30 on how ignorance of him arises and is overcome. Sandhi: वेदाहं is veda+aham (a+a→ā); चार्जुन is ca+arjuna (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत ।
सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
sentences.tr:
icchā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata |
sarva-bhūtāni saṃmoham sarge yānti parantapa ||

morph.gloss: arising from (icchā-dveṣa-samuttha: 'arising from desire and aversion', instr. sg., agreeing with dvandva-mohena)
a pair (of opposites), duality (first compound member)
delusion (dvandva-moha: 'the delusion of the pairs of opposites', instr. sg.)
to become bewildered (saṃmoha: 'delusion, bewilderment', acc. sg., object of yānti)
creation, birth (loc. sg. 'at birth, at [each] creation')
to go, fall into (yānti: present 3rd pl.)

sentences.l: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at [their] birth, O scorcher of the foe.
sentences.i: All beings fall into delusion at birth, Bhārata, through the delusion of opposites that arises from desire and aversion, scorcher of the foe.
sentences.n: Bhārata and Parantapa, both recurring epithets of Arjuna (already used repeatedly in ch.2-4). Dvandva, 'the pair, duality' — the opposites like pleasure and pain, heat and cold, cf. 2.14's śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha — arises from icchā-dveṣa, 'desire and aversion', and this dvandva-moha, 'delusion of opposites', is named as the root cause of every being's bewilderment sarge, 'at birth, at [each] creation' — the ordinary condition from which the devotees of verse 28 are freed.

sentences.t:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
sentences.tr:
yeṣām tu anta-gatam pāpam janānām puṇya-karmaṇām |
te dvandva-moha-nirmuktāḥ bhajante mām dṛḍha-vratāḥ ||

morph.gloss: gone (anta-gata: 'come to an end, exhausted', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with pāpam; tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)
deed (puṇya-karman: 'of meritorious deeds', gen. pl., agreeing with janānām)
to release, free (nirmukta: past participle, dvandva-moha-nirmukta: 'freed from the delusion of the pairs', nom. pl.; visarga dropped before bh-)
to worship, revere (bhajante: present middle 3rd pl.)
vow (dṛḍha-vrata: 'of firm vow, steadfast', nom. pl.)

sentences.l: But of whom the sin has come to an end, of people of meritorious deeds — they, freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship me, of firm vow.
sentences.i: But those people of meritorious deeds whose sin has come to an end, freed from the delusion of opposites, worship me with firm resolve.
sentences.n: This gives the positive counterpart to verse 27: janānām puṇya-karmaṇām, 'people of meritorious deeds', whose pāpam antagatam, 'sin has run its course', become dvandva-moha-nirmuktāḥ, 'freed from the delusion of opposites' just described, and so can worship Kṛṣṇa dṛḍha-vratāḥ, 'with firm vows'. Sandhi: त्वन्तगतं is tu+anta-gatam (yaṇ sandhi, u→v).

sentences.t:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये ।
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
sentences.tr:
jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye |
te brahma tat viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmam karma ca akhilam ||

morph.gloss: release (jarā-maraṇa-mokṣa: 'release from old age and death', dat. sg. of purpose)
to take refuge in (āśritya: gerund 'having taken refuge in')
who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative, subject)
brahman, kept untranslated (acc. sg. neut., object)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., in apposition to brahma; -t + v- → -d v-)
whole, entire (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with adhyātmam)
pertaining to the self, the individual self (a technical term paired with adhibhūta and adhidaiva, defined at 8.3-4; acc. sg. neut., object)
entire, whole (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma; ca + a- → cā-)

sentences.l: For release from old age and death, having taken refuge in me, those who strive — they know that brahman entire, the whole [truth of] the individual self, and action entirely.
sentences.i: Those who strive for release from old age and death, taking refuge in me, come to know brahman completely, the whole truth of the individual self, and action in its entirety.
sentences.n: Adhyātma, 'pertaining to the self, the individual self', is a technical term defined explicitly at the opening of the next chapter (8.3); here, alongside brahman (kept untranslated) and karman, 'action', it names one of the domains of complete knowledge reached by those who take refuge in Kṛṣṇa for jarā-maraṇa-mokṣa, 'release from old age and death'. This verse and the next set up, ahead of their full definition, the further terms adhibhūta and adhidaiva that open chapter 8. Sandhi: मामाश्रित्य is mām+āśritya; तद्विदुः is tat+viduḥ (-t+v-→-d v-); चाखिलम् is ca+akhilam (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः ।
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
sentences.tr:
sa-adhibhūta-adhidaivam mām sa-adhiyajñam ca ye viduḥ |
prayāṇa-kāle api ca mām te viduḥ yukta-cetasaḥ ||

morph.gloss: with, together with (prefix, first compound member; sa + a- → sā-)
pertaining to material existence, the elements (technical term defined at 8.4, second member)
pertaining to the gods, the divine order (technical term defined at 8.4, third member, agreeing with mām: 'me together with adhibhūta and adhidaiva')
with, together with (prefix; sa + a- → sā-)
pertaining to sacrifice (technical term defined at 8.4, agreeing with mām)
departure, setting forth (from the body, i.e. death) (first compound member)
time (prayāṇa-kāla: 'the time of departure', loc. sg.; kāle + a- → kāle 'pi with avagraha)
to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl.; -uḥ + y- → -ur y-)

sentences.l: Together with the elements and the divine order, me, together with sacrifice too, who know — even at the time of departure, me they know, of disciplined mind.
sentences.i: Those who know me together with the elements, the divine order, and sacrifice — being of disciplined mind, they know me even at the time of death.
sentences.n: This closes the chapter with the third technical term, adhiyajña, 'pertaining to sacrifice' (with adhibhūta and adhidaiva from verse 29); all three are given their full definitions only at the start of chapter 8, whose opening question from Arjuna repeats these very words. Prayāṇa-kāle, 'at the time of departure [from the body]', i.e. at death, names the ultimate test of this knowledge, developed at length in chapter 8's teaching on what is remembered at the moment of death. Sandhi: साधिभूताधिदैवं packs sa+adhibhūta+adhidaivam (a+a→ā twice); साधियज्ञं is sa+adhiyajñam (a+a→ā); प्रयाणकालेऽपि is kāle+api; विदुर्युक्तचेतसः is viduḥ+yukta-cetasaḥ (-uḥ+y-→-ur y-).

glossary.कश्चन: kaścana — kim-cana — anyone, anyone at all (nom. sg.; with na: 'no one at all')

glossary.द्वन्द्वमोहेन: dvandva-mohena — dvandva — a pair (of opposites), duality (first compound member); moha — delusion (dvandva-moha: 'the delusion of the pairs of opposites', instr. sg.)

glossary.येषां: yeṣām — yad — who (yeṣām: gen. pl. relative)
glossary.त्वन्तगतं: tu anta-gatam — tu — but; anta — end (first compound member); gata — gone (anta-gata: 'come to an end, exhausted', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with pāpam; tu + a- → tva-, yaṇ sandhi)

glossary.पुण्यकर्मणाम्: puṇya-karmaṇām — puṇya — meritorious (first compound member); karman — deed (puṇya-karman: 'of meritorious deeds', gen. pl., agreeing with janānām)

glossary.यतन्ति: yatanti — yat — to strive (yatanti: present 3rd pl.)

about: Chapter 7, Jñānavijñānayoga, "the yoga of knowledge and discernment," opens the Gītā's second movement: after six chapters on action, meditation and self-discipline, Kṛṣṇa turns to teach who he himself is, promising Arjuna a knowledge so complete that nothing further remains to be known once it is grasped. He describes his nature in two parts: a lower, eightfold prakṛti made of earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, understanding and ego, and a higher nature that has become the individual soul sustaining the universe. Everything that exists is strung on him like clusters of jewels on a thread; he is the sap in water, the light of sun and moon, the syllable Om in the Vedas, the seed of all beings — and yet, veiled by his own power of illusion (māyā) and by the states the three guṇas produce, he goes unrecognized by a deluded world. The chapter's central concern is who does and does not turn to him: evil-doers, their knowledge stolen by illusion, do not; but four kinds of virtuous people do — the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of gain, and the man of knowledge, the last of whom is ranked highest and called, in Kṛṣṇa's own words, his very self. Kṛṣṇa also accounts for the worship of other deities without condemning it: whatever form of god a devotee approaches with faith, it is Kṛṣṇa who steadies that faith and grants its fruit, though such fruit is merely finite, unlike the goal his own devotees reach. The chapter closes on its most quoted line, vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti, "the son of Vasudeva is everything," the rare realization of a soul perfected across many births, and ends by naming three further technical terms — adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña — whose meaning the next chapter opens by explaining.
